One IPO doesn't undo five down days or a hawkish Fed. Composite gap-risk sits at 56 (WARM) and P(≥1% gap) is ~40%, above the 35% trigger, so GREEN is locked out. The scanner boarded one name — WSM, a Type A post-earnings gap graded A, tagged bearish — but it printed on near-zero relative volume (0.01x vs the 1.3x bar) and, critically, the actual Q3 print was a double-beat with guidance reiterated, which conflicts with the bearish tag. Honor the board as watch-only; sell nothing new today and re-run tomorrow.

focus.jnote: The scanner boarded a name, but the tape is a relief bounce fighting a hawkish Fed, and the one setup is thin and self-contradictory — that's the signal. On Wednesday the S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.63, its fifth straight decline and longest losing streak since June, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42% to 24,429.88 and the Dow fell 1.11% to 50,198. Overnight the mood flipped: US stock futures rallied after Anthropic priced a record-breaking IPO, with gray-market trading indicating shares may open roughly 27% higher following the upsized $107.3 billion deal. That lifted pre-open futures — Dow futures rose 0.6%, S&P 500 futures added 1.2% and Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 2% as tech surged in premarket. But the macro backdrop is hostile to premium selling: the Fed minutes turned hawkish, with almost all officials seeing more hikes and a 25bp hike on December 9 ~95% priced in, and the 10-year yield holds above 5% with the dollar near a 19-month high. A Sniper does not open new premium into that.
focus.notdown: AI/chip names caught a strong relief bid overnight as Anthropic's record IPO reignited enthusiasm — Nasdaq-100 contracts climbed ~2.3% and the S&P 500 headed for its first daily gain in six sessions. But none of these boarded as clean Snipers, and chasing a one-day IPO-driven relief bounce in a tape that just logged five straight losses — against a hawkish Fed and a 10Y above 5% — is exactly the trap 4-VAL guards against. Watch-only.
focus.notup: WSM (Williams-Sonoma) is the scanner's boarded name, tagged bearish — and the honest problem is the tag fights the print. Q3 delivered +5.1% comps, +5.8% revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS of $2.19, growth of +11.7%, a clean double-beat vs the ~$2.16–2.21 consensus, and management reiterated fiscal 2026 guidance. That reads bullish, not bearish — yet the scanner's price feed shows a −7.8% gap on near-zero relative volume (0.01x vs the 1.3x bar), the weakest possible confirmation and likely a stale/erroneous quote. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: P(≥1% gap) at ~40% is above the 35% trigger and composite 56 is WARM — either locks out GREEN. Two: the October FOMC minutes read hawkish into a ~95%-priced December hike and the 10Y is above 5% — a rate backdrop that caps the AI-relief bounce and keeps two-sided gap risk live. Three: the one boarded name (WSM) is honored on the board but printed its gap on near-zero relative volume (0.01x) and its bearish tag conflicts with a clean double-beat and reiterated guidance — a self-contradictory, weakly-confirmed setup. Stand down on new credit spreads, treat the board as watch-only, and re-run tomorrow. Cash is a position today.

risks: Hawkish Fed & a 10-year above 5% — the October minutes turned hawkish, with almost all officials seeing more hikes and a December 9 move ~95% priced, while the 10-year holds above 5% and the dollar sits near a 19-month high. A rate backdrop this tight caps the AI-relief bounce and is a core reason the verdict is RED.

Five-day losing streak — the S&P fell for a fifth straight session to 7,323.63, its longest losing streak since June. One record IPO doesn’t reverse a trend; a failed relief bounce is the base-case risk.

Anthropic debut volatility — futures rallied on the record ~$107B IPO with shares indicated ~27% higher, but a splashy first-day debut can whipsaw the whole AI complex intraday in either direction — adds event-driven gap risk on top of the macro.

WSM setup is thin and self-contradictory — the only boarded name is tagged bearish, but Q3 was a double-beat (+5.8% revenue, EPS $2.19 up +11.7%) with guidance reiterated, and its gap printed on ~0.01x relative volume. Verify the real pre-market price and direction before treating it as anything but watch-only.

Strait of Hormuz & oil — concerns over Middle East energy-shipping disruptions amid the ongoing US–Israeli war with Iran limited oil’s losses, even as Hormuz flows recovered to near pre-war levels. Easing now on a supply surplus, but any re-escalation sends crude and the geopolitical premium vertical — a live tail.
